Executive Headteacher' blog
Welcome back to all the members of our community. After a good break fuelled by glorious weather, we have all returned with the energy and enthusiasm we thrive upon at The Beacon. With all numbers crunched and outcomes securely in, we are in the strongest of places to reflect on another successful year at The Beacon. I am immensely proud of what our pupils, staff, families and wider community have achieved together.
Nationally, the educational landscape continues to present significant challenges. Research consistently highlights the widening attainment gap. Here in Southeast Kent, these challenges are particularly evident, with our coastal communities continuing to experience some of the lowest opportunity rankings nationally. Yet, despite these barriers, our young people continue to demonstrate what can be achieved when high expectations are matched with personalised support, strong relationships and a genuine belief in every individual's potential.
At The Beacon, our vision has always extended beyond qualifications alone. Whilst accreditation and outcomes remain important, our ultimate aim is to ensure every young person leaves us ready to thrive, contribute positively to their community and live the fullest life possible. This year, our Sixth Form pupils have demonstrated exceptional progress across our five-strand curriculum – Communication, Number, Digital technology, Understanding the World and Healthy Lifestyles.
Most encouragingly, similar patterns of strong progress were seen across all areas of our schools, reflecting high levels of engagement, aspiration and commitment from our pupils. Our curriculum is designed around the skills and experiences that enable young people to lead independent, fulfilled and successful lives.
Through pathways focusing on Communication, Number, Digital Technology, Understanding the World and Healthy Lifestyles, pupils develop not only academic knowledge but also the confidence, independence and practical skills required for adulthood. For pupils accessing our Specialist Curriculum pathways, achievements have been equally impressive, with all pupils demonstrating expected or, in most cases, accelerated progress across all curriculum strands.
These achievements reflect far more than academic success. They represent growth in communication, independence, resilience, self-belief and readiness for life beyond school.
One of the most pleasing aspects of this year's outcomes is the continued success of our most vulnerable learners. National research continues to highlight significant attainment gaps for disadvantaged young people. However, at The Beacon, our Pupil Premium pupils continue to perform in line with, and often above, their peers. This reflects the impact of our whole-community approach, including personalised support from teachers, teaching assistants and our MAST staff, alongside practical family support, community initiatives and targeted interventions......relationships matter!!
We believe every child deserves the opportunity to succeed regardless of their starting point, and this year's outcomes demonstrate the power of combining ambition with genuine care and support.
Perhaps the most significant measure of our success is where our pupils go next. I am delighted to share that 100% of our Key Stage 5 leavers have secured positive destinations in further education, employment and training. This achievement significantly exceeds national outcomes for young people with Education, Health and Care Plans and reflects the strength of our Preparation for Adulthood programme and transition support.
Particularly noteworthy is the continued success of Beacon Plus, with its employability pathway. To date, every Beacon Plus leaver has progressed into employment, supported employment, volunteering with clear employment routes or further progression opportunities. These outcomes demonstrate what is possible when young people are given the right opportunities, appropriate support and meaningful pathways into adulthood.
As a school, we often speak about belonging, ambition, resilience and authenticity and this year's outcomes bring those values to life.
They tell the story of young people overcoming barriers, embracing opportunities and preparing for bright futures. They tell the story of families, staff and governors working together to create a nurturing and aspirational environment. Above all, they remind us that education must always be about much more than examination results.
Together, we continue to prove that every young person can thrive when they feel valued, supported and inspired to succeed.

Careers - Information for parents and carers
Here you will find some useful information and contact details to explain how we support our young people to get ready for their onward progression routes.
Our Aims:All pupils will have access to a wide range of information and resources related to careers and onward progression pathways appropriate to their needs.Pupils will have the opportunity to meet with a level 7 careers advisor for either a 1-1 discussion or a group discussion based on their onward progression route.Pupils will have the opportunity to participate in work experience in year 10 and 6th form appropriate to their needs.
Staff support is provided to some pupils, as required, to support them to complete a work placement.Pupils and their families will be informed about a range of opportunities available to them and will have the opportunity to meet with local providers at our Next Steps events. Pupils will be provided with opportunities to learn about different job roles and progression route, as well as learning how to write covering letters and CVs if appropriate.Some pupils will access and work towards the ASDAN accreditation as part of their curriculum offer.Pupils will be given the opportunity to develop a better understanding of their own skills and qualities and how these can be transferred into the world of work.
Pupils will be supported and reliably informed to help them prepare and make decisions about their onward progression routes.
If you would like to find out more about how we support your young person with careers and next steps at The Beacon, please speak to their form tutor or to me.
Rebecca Loynds Assistant Headteacher & Careers Lead

Careers - Information for staff and governors
As a member of The Beacon community you are at the forefront of helping our pupils prepare for their future. We all have a valuable role to play in supporting our pupils to develop their independence and prepare for adulthood. Careers advice starts in secondary, but learning all about The World of Work starts at the beginning of The Beacon learning journey in EYFS.
We have an obligation to support our pupils develop their independence, confidence and life skills, and encourage them to be as aspirational as possible.When we think of careers we aren’t necessarily always thinking about what job our pupils will do when they are older, but rather understanding more about how different people contribute to society and what that means for them.
At The Beacon we have developed a careers programme which has been weaved into our five curriculum strands.
If you would like to find out more about careers and next steps at The Beacon, please speak to me.
Rebecca LoyndsAssistant Headteacher & Careers Lead

This policy should be read in conjunction with the following school policies:
Definition of SEN
A child or young person has SEN if they have a learning difficulty or disability, which calls for special educational provision to be made for him or her.
A child of compulsory school age or a young person has a learning difficulty if he or she:(a) Has a significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of others of the same age; or(b) Has a disability which prevents or hinders him or her from making use of facilities of a kind generally provided for others of the same age in mainstream schools or mainstream post-16 institutions. SEN Code of Practice (2015, p 15).
Definition of disability
Many children and young people who have SEN may also have a disability under the Equality Act 2010 – that is ‘…a physical or mental impairment which has a long-term and substantial adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities’. This definition provides a relatively low threshold and includes more children than many realise: ‘long-term’ is defined as ‘a year or more’ and ‘substantial’ is defined as ‘more than minor or trivial’ SEN Code of Practice (2015, p16).
The Beacon, Folkestone
The Beacon Folkestone is a maintained foundation special school situated in Folkestone and caters for over 350 pupils and young people from reception through to sixth form provision. Our pupils and young people all have a current education, health and care plan (EHCP) and have a wide range of profound, severe and complex special educational needs. Special needs include autism, communication and interaction difficulties, physical difficulties and associated learning difficulties. All pupils are referred to the school by Kent County Council Assessment and Placement Service or from other local authorities with specific agreement from Kent County Council.
The Governors
The Governing Body of The Beacon Folkestone School is committed to the principle of ensuring that the school may continue to provide an excellent level of service to its community and shows an interest in all aspects of its work.
The governors, in co-operation with the Head Teacher and Head of School, determine the school’s general policy and approach to the provision for pupils with an EHCP, establish the appropriate staff and funding arrangements and maintain a monitoring oversight of the school’s work.
The Governors are particularly keen to ensure that the pupils are provided with the highest standards of accommodation and resourcing that can be made available.

The Beacon Folkestone is an essential part of the County’s special needs provision, providing a service not only to the community and its pupils, but also filling a part of the County’s continuum of service to children with SEN. Admission Criteria
Admission to The Beacon Folkestone usually follows consideration by the County Panel. Recommendation for a school place is usually based upon recognition that the pupil will make greater progress and speedier development within the curriculum and resource structures of the school. In every case a placement at The Beacon Folkestone is a positive step in furthering the pupil’s achievements. All pupils at The Beacon Folkestone have an Education Health and Care Plan that recommends placement in a special school with small teaching groups and individual learning plans.
Some pupils are transferred directly from other special schools following home moves or other special circumstances. All referrals and admissions come through Kent County Council.
Staffing
Staff across the school are dedicated to raising pupils’ attainments.
Teaching staff all work to develop and continuously enhance subject/skills based expertise, thereby acting as resource points for others as set out in our CPD policy under the “expert” level of training. Individual teachers have attended a wide range of courses including and up to post graduate and master levels. All teachers have completed or are on a pathway to complete teacher training, the exception to this are a specific small cohort of unqualified tutors who are recruited for their specifically identifiable and unique skillset (such as outdoor pursuits/education). HLTAs and TAs also follow our expert and entitlement training courses.
The continuous development of a highly skilled Teaching Assistant Team is a priority as they lead learning sessions for pupils.
Assessment
The Code of Practice emphasises the need to identify pupils at the earliest possible time. Before a pupil comes to The Beacon Folkestone a member of teaching staff will visit pupils at their school or nursery to discuss the pupil’s needs and observe the pupil in situ.
Pupils are assessed on admission, usually over a 6–12 week period with their initial assessments forming a baseline assessment that is tracked to demonstrate the progress they make during their time with us.

The results of these reviews are available to all staff. Whole school data (attainment and progress) occur in line to follow the formal assessment cycle. Careers - Information for Employers
Why work with a pupil from The Beacon?
Would you like to work with an outstanding school? Would you like to work with inspiring young people? Do you have a business that could provide a pupil with a work placement? Are you an employer that could come and deliver a workshop in our school? If the answer is yes to any of these questions then we would love to hear from you.
Pupils at The Beacon participate in an inclusive careers programme from EYFS through to year 14. This includes work experience appropriate to their age and ability. It includes careers advice, careers workshops and employer encounters. Pupils at The Beacon are motivated, polite, hardworking and keen to learn. They are all on their own journey to adulthood, enjoy learning new things and meeting new people.
Some of our pupils need a bit more help than others, but we know when they are provided with opportunities that are meaningful and work for them, they go on to do amazing things!
Rebecca LoyndsAssistant Headteacher & Careers Lead

Careers - Information for pupils
Message from Assistant Headteacher for Zone 3 and Careers Lead
At The Beacon, you will be provided with opportunities to learn about a range of jobs, placements, internships, apprenticeships, social care and onward progression routes to prepare you for your next steps into adulthood. You will have the opportunity and support to discuss and think about your next steps and what is your best onward route. This is a fantastic opportunity for you to really think about what your life will be like as an adult.
All staff at The Beacon are here to support your transition into your onward route. They are able to provide you with the best help and advice you need to support you making these exciting decisions. You will study Life Skills, Employability, your chosen subject options, as well as being able to access the community and develop your confidence and understanding of The World of Work.You will have the opportunity to meet visitors and experience employer encounters, who will come in and discuss job opportunities and careers with you.
Where appropriate, you will participate in work experience in year 10 and again in the 6th form. These placements are designed to meet your needs and aspirations.
You will also get dedicated time to talk to our trained careers advisor (Mel Winter) to discuss your next steps.
If you would like to find out more about how we support you with careers and next steps at The Beacon, please speak to your form tutor or to me.
Rebecca LoyndsAssistant Headteacher & Careers Lead

Kent Special Educational Needs Trust (KsENT)
We are very proud to be a founder member of KsENT, a Cooperative Trust made up of eight Kent Special schools committed to formally working together to support and develop our schools and the education they provide. Nine more SEN schools are currently consulting on joining the Trust which will mean that over 75% of the County’s SEN schools will be members. The other five schools plan to join the Trust by September 2017, giving special schools a single, cohesive focus and a real mandate to develop provision across the county.
Co-operative Schools Network (CSNet)
We are proud to be a school built around cooperative values and are working alongside other cooperative alliances in London and the South East to collaborate in developing provision for our young people. CSNet is the network that joins us all together!
